title: Adaptive Cluster-Based Normalization for Robust TOPSIS in Multicriteria Decision-Making
tldr: An adaptive cluster-based normalization method combining fuzzy-number clustering with logarithmic normalization improves TOPSIS ranking stability and outlier robustness in multicriteria decision-making.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional TOPSIS normalization techniques such as Min-Max and Z-score struggle with datasets containing outliers, large variances, or skewed distributions, leading to biased rankings. Conventional clustering methods impose rigid, data-driven categories that misclassify alternatives sharing features with multiple groups. There is a lack of studies combining fuzzy clustering with centroid-based distance allocation and logarithmic normalization within MCDM frameworks.
approach: Introduced Clustering Using Fuzzy Numbers and Centroid-Based Distance Allocation, where expert-defined ideal cluster centroids replace data-driven centroid computation.
Alternatives are represented as triangular fuzzy numbers (a, b, c) and converted to crisp centroid values using the arithmetic mean of the three components.
Euclidean distance between alternative centroids and predefined cluster centroids determines cluster assignment via minimum-distance criterion.
Integrated logarithmic normalization X = (log(X) - log(Xmin)) / (log(Xmax) - log(Xmin)) within each cluster before TOPSIS ranking.
Weights for each criterion per cluster are derived directly from normalized cluster centroids, eliminating subjective weighting procedures.
Applied the method to a case study of 12 Asian cities evaluated on four criteria: cost, infrastructure, safety, and accessibility.
Compared the proposed method against Fuzzy K-Means clustering, Min-Max normalization, and standard TOPSIS as baselines.
findings: Proposed clustering method and Fuzzy K-Means produced nearly identical assignments for 11 of 12 cities, with the proposed method more logically classifying City K into Cluster 1.
Logarithmic and Min-Max normalizations produced nearly identical TOPSIS outcomes when no significant outliers were present.
num: In Cluster 3, City E scored 0.747 under Min-Max but 0.886 under logarithmic normalization, showing 18.6% improvement in ranking stability with outliers.
num: City C achieved a perfect TOPSIS score of 1.000 under both normalization methods in Cluster 2.
num: City K consistently scored approximately 0.887 across both normalization methods as the top alternative in Cluster 1.
The proposed clustering method is deterministic, computationally simpler, and avoids iterative recalculation compared to Fuzzy K-Means.
Logarithmic normalization compresses extreme values and prevents any single criterion from dominating the TOPSIS ranking.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes two methodological innovations to the MCDM field: a fuzzy-number-based clustering approach with expert-defined centroid profiles and logarithmic normalization for TOPSIS. The clustering method decouples cluster definition from data distribution, enabling deterministic, transparent, and computationally efficient classification compared to iterative methods like Fuzzy K-Means. The logarithmic normalization technique provides a robust alternative to Min-Max and Z-score methods, particularly effective in handling outliers and high-variance datasets. Together, these methods improve the accuracy and stability of TOPSIS rankings without adding implementation complexity, offering a scalable framework applicable across diverse decision-making domains including logistics, finance, environmental planning, and strategic prioritization.
directly_justifies: Logarithmic normalization compresses extreme values and preserves proportional differences, improving ranking stability in TOPSIS.
Expert-defined cluster centroids allow decision-makers to define ideal profiles independently of the dataset for context-aware classification.
Proposed clustering method achieves nearly identical results to Fuzzy K-Means with significantly lower computational overhead.
City E showed 18.6% higher TOPSIS score under logarithmic normalization (0.886) versus Min-Max (0.747) in the presence of outliers.
Weights are derived directly from cluster centroids, eliminating the need for subjective weighting procedures.
limits: The definition of ideal cluster centroids relies on expert judgment, which may introduce subjectivity into the clustering process.
Performance in large-scale or high-dimensional problems has not been tested.
Applicability has been demonstrated only within the TOPSIS framework; integration with VIKOR, PROMETHEE, and AHP remains unexplored.
Case study uses only 12 alternatives and 4 criteria, limiting generalizability to larger real-world datasets.

limitations: Expert-defined cluster centroids introduce subjectivity that may affect reproducibility and consistency across different decision-makers.
Case study limited to 12 alternatives and 4 criteria; scalability to large-scale or high-dimensional problems is unvalidated.
Applicability tested only within TOPSIS framework; generalizability to other MCDM models such as VIKOR, PROMETHEE, and AHP is unproven.
No sensitivity analysis on how variations in expert-defined fuzzy centroid values affect final cluster assignments and rankings.
remember_this: Fuzzy-number clustering with expert-defined centroids achieves nearly identical results to Fuzzy K-Means with lower computational cost.
Logarithmic normalization performs equally to Min-Max on clean data but outperforms it when outliers are present.
